newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba has no inclination to cut discount rate - Hesse.
newsitem.headline: Buba has no inclination to cut discount rate - Hesse.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Thursday that the Bundesbank council had no inclination to cut the German discount rate to one percent from its current 2.5 percent.

Hesse made the comment during a speech at a Hannover university. His statement comes after the finance minister of the German state of Lower Saxony Andreas Fischer demanded such a cut in the discount rate.

Hesse also said that the Bundesbank was determined to stay on a course of stability until December 31, 1998, when it is due to hand over monetary policy responsibility to the planned European Central Bank.
Hesse added that the flow of marks out of Germany had stopped, but that no inflow was yet noticable.
He said that should this tendency continue, then the dollar would climb noticably.
